headline: 10 years' jail for damaging July Uprising Memorial Museum artefacts
summary: The July Uprising Memorial Museum Act introduces strict penalties for those who harm the museum's collections.
details: The July Uprising Memorial Museum Act has been introduced to protect the artefacts and collections of the museum.
Under the new law, anyone found damaging the museum's artefacts or properties will face up to 10 years of imprisonment.
The act aims to preserve the history of the July uprising for future generations by ensuring the safety of its physical records.
The law establishes a strict legal framework to prevent vandalism and the theft of historical items related to the uprising.
caption:
10 years in prison for damaging a museum artefact. The July Uprising Memorial Museum Act is here.

The July Uprising Memorial Museum Act has been introduced to protect the artefacts and collections of the museum.

Under the new law, anyone found damaging the museum's artefacts or properties will face up to 10 years of imprisonment.

The act aims to preserve the history of the July uprising for future generations by ensuring the safety of its physical records.

The law establishes a strict legal framework to prevent vandalism and the theft of historical items related to the uprising.

headline_marked: Hasan Mahmud's 6-wicket haul [[bundles Australia out for 198]] in Darwin
headline: Hasan Mahmud's 6-wicket haul bundles Australia out for 198 in Darwin
summary: Pacer Hasan Mahmud claims a career-best 6/55 to lead Bangladesh's bowling attack as they dominate Day 1 of the first Test.
details: Pacer Hasan Mahmud became the first Bangladeshi bowler to take a five-wicket haul in Australia, claiming career-best figures of 6 for 55 in 17 overs.
His relentless pressure helped bundle out the hosts for 198 on Day 1 of the first Test at Marrara Stadium in Darwin.
Hasan's dominance included removing key batters like Steve Smith (71) and Nathan Lyon, ensuring Australia's tail was quickly exposed.
Supporting the attack, Ebadot Hossain and Taskin Ahmed each claimed two wickets, maintaining pressure throughout the sessions.
Ebadot provided a crucial breakthrough by bowling Alex Carey (19), breaking a dangerous 56-run partnership with Steve Smith.
Taskin Ahmed further tightened the grip by castling Beau Webster (12), preventing any significant recovery for the Australian side.
Despite a resilient 45th Test half-century from Steve Smith, the Tigers' pacers remained dominant across all three sessions.
Australia had struggled from the early stages, reduced to 74 for 4 at lunch, before eventually being dismissed for 198.
caption:
A historic 6-wicket haul! Hasan Mahmud destroys Australia's batting lineup in Darwin.

Pacer Hasan Mahmud became the first Bangladeshi bowler to take a five-wicket haul in Australia, claiming career-best figures of 6 for 55 in 17 overs.

His relentless pressure helped bundle out the hosts for 198 on Day 1 of the first Test at Marrara Stadium in Darwin.

Hasan's dominance included removing key batters like Steve Smith (71) and Nathan Lyon, ensuring Australia's tail was quickly exposed.

Supporting the attack, Ebadot Hossain and Taskin Ahmed each claimed two wickets, maintaining pressure throughout the sessions.

Ebadot provided a crucial breakthrough by bowling Alex Carey (19), breaking a dangerous 56-run partnership with Steve Smith.

Taskin Ahmed further tightened the grip by castling Beau Webster (12), preventing any significant recovery for the Australian side.

Despite a resilient 45th Test half-century from Steve Smith, the Tigers' pacers remained dominant across all three sessions.

Australia had struggled from the early stages, reduced to 74 for 4 at lunch, before eventually being dismissed for 198.
